# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual module through `view.model`, plus histories and metadata through the wrapper. It discovers `sample_batch` in the module’s defining Python module to retrieve corruption bookkeeping.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors with matching B × L shapes. The probe validates token ranges, score shapes, and finite supervised margins. Feature probes use evaluation mode without gradients and restore the previous training mode.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Directional alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 real-item embeddings, excluding padding and MASK. Mean pairwise cosine is mapped to [0,1]; higher indicates stronger alignment, without proving collapse.
- **Representation geometry:** Separately samples up to 256 items and users. Reports raw norms, centered variance, centered singular values, and RankMe effective rank. Narrow spectra suggest limited representational variation; no universal healthy threshold is supplied.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Across up to ten batches, computes mean margin, tenth-percentile margin, negative-wins rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger sampled training separation.
- **Coverage and allocation:** Counts valid targets, terminal targets, observed input types, and matched corruption branches. Optional runtime training counters describe branch allocation; coefficient shares do not measure gradient shares.

# Perturbation & Tests

The geometry probe appends MASK to histories, matching inference-style readout. Margin probes inspect sampler-corrupted inputs and identify mask/random/unchanged branches only when bookkeeping matches exactly. There are no paired perturbation or causal sensitivity tests.
